scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: Hello, I'm on PC0 (20.1.1.x). I can't get through to
PC12 (120.1.1.x) on the far side of the network any more -- it times out
every time. I vaguely remember hearing our two sides run on "different
routing" somehow, but I honestly don't know what that means. Could someone
take a look at whatever connects the two sides and fix it? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
End-to-end connectivity between the two endpoints is healthy. I validated from both sides: pc0 (20.1.1.10) successfully reaches pc12 (120.1.1.10) and vice versa with 0% loss and sub‑millisecond RTTs over multiple probes. This confirms the forwarding plane and the interconnecting routing between the two “sides” are functioning, and there’s no evidence of a broken link, misrouted prefixes, or a downed routing process in the path.

Mechanism: Because ICMP echo/echo-reply traverses all intermediate routers, successful pings both directions prove that routing adjacencies, route distribution between domains, and ARP/ND resolution on both LANs are currently correct. If there were a routing break between the domains, we would observe packet loss or asymmetry; we do not.

Localization: No specific device or interface shows impact. The tested path spans from pc0.eth0 (E) through the routed core to pc12.eth0 (GG), and traffic returns cleanly.

Root cause: Not reproducible at this time; the earlier timeouts were likely transient or related to an application/service on pc12 rather than the network path (e.g., host firewall or service port not listening).

Corrective fix: No network changes required. Please retry your original workflow. If the issue is with a specific application/port (not just ping), let us know the protocol/port so we can test TCP/UDP reachability (e.g., curl/iperf) and, if needed, coordinate with the pc12 owner to verify host firewall and service status.
